newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin says cutting debt 'ultimate goal'.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin says cutting debt 'ultimate goal'.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Thursday the Liberal government's ultimate goal, once a balanced budget was achieved, would be to cut the size of the debt in relation to gross domestic product.
But he said that if the economy were in the middle of a downturn, it might not be the time to pay off debt.
Economists widely expect a balanced budget in two years or a little more. Asked at an economists' conference what the government would do once the budget was balanced, Martin said:

"The ultimate goal as far as I'm concerned is what will bring the debt-to-GDP ratio down the quickest. The decision to be made at that time is going to be dependent totally on the economic circumstances of the time.

"In other words, if we're in the middle of a massive boom, I'm not sure that's the time for stimulative spending or a stimulative tax cut. If we're in the middle of a huge downturn, then the answer may be substantially different."

He repeated that for the current fiscal year, which ends on March 31, the government would hit its deficit target or do better. Last month he revised his projection down to C$19.0 billion from an earlier projected C$24.3 billion.
